title: Ambition Content Emergency Plan
summary: Emergency content strategy for Ambition Mechanical social media launch.
content:
Ambition Mechanical: Content Emergency Plan

Author: Alex (Deal Architect) Date: 2026-03-12 Status: Strategy brief. No posts or client contact without Patrik approval.

The Situation

  • $2k/month retainer promises social media management
  • 4+ weeks with zero posts published on any platform
  • 6 LinkedIn drafts ready (Tony, Mar 9): projects/content-agent/output/ambition/first-linkedin-post-drafts.md
  • 4 LinkedIn Training Day drafts ready (Tony, Mar 9): projects/content-agent/output/ambition/training-day-posts.md
  • 14 Reel briefs + 4 LinkedIn video briefs ready (Cleo, Mar 9): projects/content-agent/briefs/ambition-briefs.md
  • Tony is blocked (Docker Desktop not installed, Postiz unusable)
  • Ash has LinkedIn credentials
  • Client is paying. Client is NOT receiving what they're paying for.
  • Upsell from $2k to $3.5k is impossible while delivering nothing

Part 1: Emergency Posting Plan (This Week, Mar 12-14)

The goal: break the silence. Get at least 3 posts live by end of week. Momentum over perfection.

What can go up RIGHT NOW (text-only LinkedIn posts, zero editing required)

These 10 LinkedIn drafts are written, approved-format, and ready to copy-paste:

First Post (pick one):

  • Option A: "We've Been Here" (82 words, strongest credibility angle)
  • Option B: "The Work You Don't See" (83 words, pairs with Primrose video)
  • Option C: "We Show Up Different" (78 words, most direct)

Recommendation: Post Option A ("We've Been Here") as the inaugural post. It acknowledges the silence ("we never had a LinkedIn page because we were too busy doing the work") and turns it into strength. After 4 weeks dark, this framing is honest and authentic.

Training Day Posts (pick one for each page):

  • Mo's Personal Page: Option A or B (first-person, signed by Mo)
  • Ambition Business Page: Option A or B (company "we" voice)

Proposed This-Week Schedule

Day Platform Post Who Posts
Thu Mar 13 LinkedIn (Ambition page) First Post: Option A "We've Been Here" Ash or Patrik (manual)
Fri Mar 14 LinkedIn (Mo's personal) Training Day: Mo Option A Ash or Patrik (manual)
Fri Mar 14 LinkedIn (Ambition page) Training Day: Business Option A Ash or Patrik (manual)

Why these three:

  1. "We've Been Here" breaks the ice on the business page. It's the reset post.
  2. Training Day content is time-relevant (already happened). Posting it weeks later starts looking stale. Use it now.
  3. LinkedIn is text-first. No video editing required. No Tony, no Docker, no Postiz needed. Just copy, paste, post.

Part 2: Who Posts?

Tony is blocked indefinitely until Docker Desktop gets installed. That's not happening this week. Here are the realistic options:

Option A: Ash Posts Manually (Recommended)

  • Ash has LinkedIn credentials
  • Ash is already on the Ambition account for day-to-day
  • LinkedIn posting = 5 minutes per post. Copy text from the drafts, paste, add hashtags, publish
  • No tools needed. Just a browser and the login.
  • This is the fastest path. One text to Ash: "Post these three this week."

Option B: Patrik Posts Manually

  • Patrik can do it but shouldn't have to. His time is better spent on ISA, IH, KOHRS.
  • Only if Ash can't or won't.

Option C: LinkedIn Native Scheduling

  • LinkedIn has built-in post scheduling (click the clock icon next to "Post")
  • Ash or Patrik could schedule all 3 posts in one 15-minute session
  • Best for: setting up next week's posts in advance once this week's emergency is handled

Option D: Install Docker Desktop and Unblock Tony

  • 5-minute install. Unblocks Tony permanently.
  • But this doesn't solve THIS WEEK. Tony still needs Postiz configured and Facebook Dev App for IG OAuth.
  • Docker install is the right move for the medium term. Not the emergency fix.

Verdict: Ash posts manually this week. Docker install happens whenever Patrik has 5 minutes. Both tracks run in parallel.

Part 3: Content Calendar (Next 2 Weeks, Mar 17-28)

Week of Mar 17-21

Shift from emergency to rhythm. Target: 2 LinkedIn posts/week (contractual) + begin Reels if any are edited.

Day Platform Content Source Editing Required
Mon Mar 17 LinkedIn (Ambition) First Post Option B or C (whichever wasn't used) first-linkedin-post-drafts.md None
Tue Mar 18 LinkedIn (Mo personal) Training Day Mo Option B training-day-posts.md None
Wed Mar 19 LinkedIn (Ambition) Training Day Business Option B training-day-posts.md None
Thu Mar 20 LinkedIn (Ambition) LI 01: Din Tai Fung Case Study (text + video) ambition-briefs.md, Brief LI 01 YES: video edit needed
Fri Mar 21 IG/TikTok Reel 01: Emergency Response Story ambition-briefs.md, Brief 01 YES: 20-30s edit from Abraza footage

Note: Thu and Fri require video editing. If no editing happens, replace with text-only LinkedIn posts. We have 10 written drafts. Better to post text than post nothing.

Week of Mar 24-28

Day Platform Content Source Editing Required
Mon Mar 24 LinkedIn (Ambition) LI 02: Backbone of Every Build ambition-briefs.md, Brief LI 02 YES: video edit
Tue Mar 25 IG/TikTok Reel 02: Primrose Progress Update ambition-briefs.md, Brief 02 YES: 30-40s cut from downloaded footage
Wed Mar 26 IG/TikTok Reel 03: Din Tai Fung Kitchen ambition-briefs.md, Brief 03 YES: 25-35s edit
Thu Mar 27 LinkedIn (Ambition) LI 03: Emergency Response Case Study ambition-briefs.md, Brief LI 03 YES: video edit
Fri Mar 28 IG/TikTok Reel 04: What Commercial Mechanical Looks Like ambition-briefs.md, Brief 04 YES: 20-30s multi-clip edit

Fallback Rule

If a video post isn't edited in time, swap it for the next unused text-only LinkedIn draft. The 10 written drafts are the safety net. The contract says 2 LinkedIn posts/week. We can hit that number with pure text while building toward Reels.

Content Inventory (What's in the Bank)

Type Count Source Editing Needed
LinkedIn text drafts (first post) 3 options first-linkedin-post-drafts.md None
LinkedIn text drafts (training day, Mo personal) 2 options training-day-posts.md None
LinkedIn text drafts (training day, business page) 2 options training-day-posts.md None
Reel briefs (with downloaded footage) 7 briefs ambition-briefs.md, Reels 01-07 YES
Reel briefs (need new footage or cloud download) 7 briefs ambition-briefs.md, Reels 08-14 YES + footage needed
LinkedIn video briefs 4 briefs ambition-briefs.md, LI 01-04 YES

Total ready-to-post content (no editing): 7 text posts Total content with editing: 18 additional pieces (11 Reels + 4 LI videos + overflow)

The 7 text posts alone cover 3.5 weeks of LinkedIn at 2/week. That buys time to get video editing flowing.

Part 4: Client Communication

Should AOM proactively message Mo?

Yes. But timing matters.

Do NOT message Mo about the gap until at least 3 posts are live. Messaging now, before anything is published, just highlights the failure with nothing to show for it. The play:

  1. This week (Mar 12-14): Post the 3 emergency posts. Say nothing to Mo.
  2. Early next week (Mar 17-18): Once 3+ posts are live, send a proactive update.

What to say (draft for Patrik/Ash to send)

After 3+ posts are live:

Mo, wanted to give you an update. We've started rolling out LinkedIn content for Ambition. You'll see the first posts are up on the business page and your personal page.

We took a bit longer than planned on the initial setup because we wanted to make sure the voice and positioning were right. The content plan is built out for the next few weeks: LinkedIn authority posts going up consistently, and Reels for Instagram and TikTok ramping up as we get the video edits flowing.

If you have any new footage from recent job sites, send it over. The more we have, the more we can push out.

Let us know if there's anything specific you want highlighted.

Why this framing works

  • Acknowledges the delay without apologizing or over-explaining
  • "Took longer on setup" is true (voice research, brief creation, drafts written)
  • Shows the plan is real and already in motion
  • Asks for footage (keeps Mo engaged and responsible for input)
  • Doesn't promise a number. Just "consistently" and "ramping up"
  • Keeps the tone confident. AOM is not behind. AOM is deliberate.

What NOT to say

  • Don't say "we had technical issues" (that's our problem, not his)
  • Don't promise 5 Reels/week immediately (we can't deliver that yet)
  • Don't bring up the retainer price or upsell (wrong moment)

Part 5: Path to Full Delivery

The contract promises 5 Reels/week + 2 LinkedIn posts/week. We're at 0/0. Here's how we ramp:

Week LinkedIn Posts Reels Notes
Mar 12-14 (this week) 3 (text) 0 Emergency catch-up
Mar 17-21 3 (2 text + 1 video) 1 First video content
Mar 24-28 2 (video-driven) 3 Editing rhythm established
Mar 31+ 2/week 4-5/week Full delivery target

Critical dependency: Video editing. Nobody is editing Ambition Reels right now. Ash has KOHRS and IH post-production. Patrik has ISA and Skylar. The Reel briefs exist but they need someone cutting footage.

Options to solve the editing bottleneck:

  1. Ash edits 2-3 quick Reels during KOHRS editing blocks (they use similar skills)
  2. Patrik blocks one 2-hour session for Ambition Reels this week
  3. Mo films vertical content on his phone and sends it. Short-form phone footage needs minimal editing.
  4. Long-term: Tony gets unblocked and handles social posting while a human handles the editing

Decision Points for Patrik

  1. Approve the 3 emergency posts for this week? (Option A first post + both Training Day posts)
  2. Who posts: Ash or Patrik? (Recommendation: Ash)
  3. Approve the client communication draft? (Send after 3 posts are live)
  4. Who edits Reels? The briefs are done. The footage is downloaded. Someone needs to cut.
  5. Install Docker Desktop this week? (5 minutes, unblocks Tony permanently)
